title: Synchronized Inventory Dashboard
problem: Inconsistent stock displays across different UI widgets lead to customer confusion and overselling.
solution: Utilize React's state lifting pattern to maintain a single source of truth for inventory counts, ensuring all UI components reflect the same data via one-way data flow.
steps: Identify the common parent component that encompasses all inventory display widgets.
Move the inventory count state variable from individual child components to the parent.
Define an event handler function in the parent to update the state.
Pass the current count and the handler function down to child components as props.
Update child components to read the count from props and trigger the handler on interaction.
outcome: A unified interface where every stock widget updates simultaneously, providing a consistent user experience.
limitation: Prop drilling can occur if state must be passed through many layers of intermediate components, which can be checked by monitoring component depth and complexity.

questions.question: In Synchronized Inventory Dashboard, why is state lifting the preferred solution?
options: It prevents multiple components from having conflicting, independent stock values.
It automatically syncs data with the backend database without extra code.
It allows components to bypass the one-way data flow constraint.
It eliminates the need for event handlers in child components.
questions.explanation: Lifting state ensures a single source of truth, preventing the inconsistency described in the problem.
questions.evidence: Inconsistent stock displays across different UI widgets lead to customer confusion and overselling.

questions.question: What is a potential limitation of the implementation in Synchronized Inventory Dashboard?
options: The browser will crash if state is updated too frequently.
Prop drilling may occur if the component tree becomes too deep.
React requires all components to share the same state.
Event handlers cannot be passed as props in React.
questions.explanation: Prop drilling is a known trade-off when moving state up through multiple layers of components.
questions.evidence: Prop drilling can occur if state must be passed through many layers of intermediate components, which can be checked by monitoring component depth and complexity.
